Default: disabled. Uses RRT room temperature for body response in supported Build 42.21.0 singleplayer and multiplayer. Warmth uses native thermoregulation; missing cold uses bounded core and regional skin corrections. Multiplayer corrections are server-owned while native simulation continues. Vehicle cabins retain the normal game body response. Multiplayer metabolism, drying and thermal damage retain native behavior.

Default: Dashboard.
Off: vanilla dashboard, no remote garage-door controls.
Dashboard: garage-door buttons and redesigned fuel gauge on the dashboard.
Heating view: larger garage-door buttons in the vehicle heating panel; vanilla dashboard.
Existing saved links are retained. Reload the world and reconnect clients after changing this setting.

Propane consumption as a percentage of the original consumption.
100% represents calculated realistic consumption.
The 18 kW heating output remains unchanged.

Maximum number of individual perishable food items tracked by RRT cold-storage rooms, including fully frozen food. The total limit is shared by all cold-storage rooms.
Default: 512 per room / 1,024 total.
Food beyond either limit does not receive RRT refrigeration or freezing.
WARNING: Higher limits increase CPU and memory usage and may cause stuttering or delayed food updates, especially in singleplayer.
Lowering the limit may leave some previously tracked food outside RRT processing after restart.

Default: disabled. Enables server diagnostics and administrator-only Heating Info, Heater Info and temperature overlay tools (also available in singleplayer). WARNING: diagnostic collection and logging may increase server load and cause lag. Use only for troubleshooting. Disabled skips optional debug collection; normal heating simulation and multiplayer synchronization still run. Restart the server/world and reconnect clients after changing this option.

Default: RRT clock.
Vanilla clock: RRT leaves the game's clock alone.
No clock: hides the game's on-screen clock.
RRT clock: replaces the game's clock with RRT's own clock, which shows the room temperature RRT simulates. Right-click it to change its colours.
Lua Digital Watch UI is optional. If it is loaded, its clock is shown in every mode and displays the RRT temperature.

Default: disabled. Removes vanilla's automatic 22°C indoor temperature baseline while city power is available, including heating in cold weather and cooling in hot weather. Room temperatures follow RRT's simulation, including heaters, insulation and outdoor weather. Electricity and original room lighting follow the normal power supply.

Default: disabled. Generators use RRT behavior: they must be connected to a nearby building from their Generator menu. During a power outage a connected generator powers only the building's electric devices. The game's "Generator tile range" is set to 1. Disabled: generators work exactly as in vanilla. While the mod LG Extended Electricity is loaded, generators always follow vanilla and LG, whatever this setting.

1%: original vanilla fuel use (default).
100%: calculated realism level, 112x original fuel use.
Values between 1 and 100 scale evenly; 50% is about 56x.

Realism is approximate, based on electrical load estimates.
Includes idle consumption and all loads.

Reload the world after changes.
Before removing RRT, set 1% and load/save.

Default: 6. Maximum horizontal distance in tiles between a heat pump's indoor and outdoor unit, and between Frostline CR-65 units. Levels do not count, so an indoor unit in a basement or bunker can connect to an outdoor unit on the ground or a flat roof above it. Lowering this value stops existing systems whose units are farther apart, and their panel shows "Line too long", until they are moved closer and connected again.

Default: disabled. Replaces the character Temperature tab with the RRT view, body-part comparison and core-temperature history. History collects while the window is closed: a 15-minute window, sampled every 5 seconds at normal speed, following game speed and pauses. Building and vehicle entry/exit markers are detected at sampling time. History is held in memory for the current session only. Does not change temperature simulation or enable Body Temperature Rework. Disable to restore the vanilla view and stop history collection.

Two-tile high-wall refrigeration evaporator. Connect the matching CR-65C outdoor unit, then use its unit controls to select Fridge or Freezer.

Two-tile condensing unit on a concrete base. Needs a solid floor open to the sky: the ground, a flat roof or an outdoor floor, not a sloped roof. Requires a matching CR-65E evaporator within the heat pump line range (sandbox, default six tiles) horizontally, on any level.
Wall-mounted breaker panel for one building: five circuits and MAIN. Mount on an inside wall; one per building is enough.

Build a hot-water radiator against an interior wall. It begins disconnected and cold. Connecting requires empty pipes, including pressure water; reservoir water and heating switches do not prevent connection.

Build an indoor propane boiler against an exterior wall. Connect radiators and fill the water loop. Add an actual propane tank, or mount a four-tank rack after removing the onboard tank, then restart manually.

Build an empty four-tank wall rack directly above an existing south-facing central heating station on the same square. Remove the station tank first. Add actual propane tanks through its controls; they feed the station one at a time. One direction is available initially.

Build a double-width hot-water radiator on two adjacent wall squares in the same room. Maximum output 3 kW at a 50°C water-to-room temperature difference; radiator water 4 L. Connect to a drained central heating loop.
Wall unit. Outside face of a solid wall (no window, door or fence), up to two levels above ground; can be fitted from below.
Wall unit. Outside face of a solid wall (no window, door or fence), up to two levels above ground; can be fitted from below.

Ground unit on a concrete base. Needs a solid floor open to the sky: the ground, a flat roof or an outdoor floor. On a sloped roof, remove the roof tiles and lay a floor first. One rotation (facing south).
